title: Green-eyed monster or green-eyed mirage? A new procedure for telling when begrudging others' success is or is not envy
heading: Green-eyed monster or green-eyed mirage?
subtitle: A new procedure for telling when begrudging others' success is or is not envy
description: Eight studies introduce a third-party criterion for testing whether an observed effect is specifically attributable to envy.
summary: Across eight studies (N = 1,507), this paper develops a third-party criterion for testing whether an observed effect is attributable specifically to envy. It checks whether the same elicitor affects uninvolved observers, providing a comparison for interpreting the effect.
finding: Deservingness effects failed the criterion; audience-valuation effects passed. The criterion addresses whether a particular effect is envy-specific, rather than establishing what an instrument measures in general.

title: Are self-conscious emotions about the self? Testing competing theories of shame and guilt across two disparate cultures
heading: Are self-conscious emotions about the self?
subtitle: Testing competing theories of shame and guilt across two disparate cultures
citation_authors: Landers, M., Sznycer, D., & Durkee, P. K.
equal_authors: Mitchell Landers and Daniel Sznycer contributed equally (joint first authors).
description: Cross-cultural tests of competing theories of shame and guilt using experiments and structural equation models with US and Indian participants (N = 853).
summary: This paper tests competing theories of shame and guilt using experimental manipulations and structural equation models with participants in the United States and India (N = 853). The research uses preregistered tests to distinguish the theories' predictions across two cultural settings.
extra_label: Supplement and code (shared by Sznycer Lab)

title: The evolution of shame and its display
heading: The evolution of shame and its display
subtitle: A theoretical review of shame, social devaluation, and emotional display
description: A theoretical review synthesizing evidence on shame, the threat of social devaluation, and the functions of shame's characteristic display.
summary: This theoretical review synthesizes evidence on shame and its characteristic display. It examines shame as a response to the threat of social devaluation and considers how posture, gaze, and speech may help limit reputational damage.
card_detail: Evidence synthesis · Social devaluation · Emotional display
